title: Harness self-check (CD-5): walking to a THING, and pressing interact only when there is one
_comment_evidence_lane: Section H/G evidence split, owner decision 2026-08-27. This self-check has no prescribed capture and exists to prove the harness can drive the game; it is the logic lane by design. Declaring it turns the continuous record off explicitly rather than leaving it to record_default_hz, which is what made a logic-only self-check trip the capture pre-flight.
_comment: NOT a protocol segment. This is the regression coverage defect CD-5 asks for by name -- "walk to Grandpa, to a harvest node and to a wild creature, asserting the prompt each time" -- exercising `move_to_entity`, `interact_with` and `advance_dialogue_until_closed` against the real Meadows. A unit test that mocked an entity would pass on a harness that walks nowhere.
_comment_where_the_world_boots: Booting meadows_playground.tscn puts the player IN GRANDPA'S BED, INSIDE THE HOUSE. This segment's own first two runs found that: `BedPrompt` offers "Get up" at t=63 s, and after getting up, 6000 navigator-driven walking frames toward a villager 44 m away left the player oscillating inside a four-metre box around (-22.6, -15) with heading swinging 73 -> -21 -> 69 -> 89 degrees and ZERO frames held -- locomotion was never disabled, the walk simply could not find the door. `stick_navigator.gd` is the repo's one walker that detours around geometry and its own header says every straight-line walk in this project failed on the same village wall; leaving a building is past what it does. That is a finding about the walker, recorded in ralph/reports/gate-f-rig-log.md, and it is not what this segment is for.
_comment_why_diag: So the segment teleports out of the house, and says so. Same precedent and same reasoning as `selfcheck_walk`: an instrument check must not become a test of the opening sequence or of a building's navmesh. The teleport is marked `diag: true`, is recorded as a teleport, and resets the distance accumulators so nothing about the jump reaches a pacing figure. Everything this segment actually measures -- entity resolution, 3D arrival, the prompt assertion, the dialogue predicate -- happens on foot after it.
_comment_why_tam: Tam, not Mira. `village_npcs.json` moved Mira INDOORS in OF31 (she stands behind her counter inside cottage_a at [18.99, -1.01]), which would make this segment fail on the same doorway again. Tam is outdoors at [8, -16], "south of the well, by the yard fence toward Grandpa's" -- open ground, a short walk from the drop point, and he opens a real conversation.

steps.title: boot the real Meadows
steps.expected: the real world scene stands up with the village cast placed

steps.title: input is in the world before anything is pressed
steps.expected: input_context is 'world'. This is the seam: every step below presses or walks, and if a modal owns input none of them mean what they say.

steps.title: an entity that is not in the world is a FAIL, not an arrival
steps.expected: FAIL naming the search. A coordinate walk cannot tell 'I arrived and nothing was here' from 'I arrived'; this step exists to prove the entity walk can.
steps.observation: EXPECTED FAIL: negative control for _find_entity. A PASS means the resolver matched something it should not have.

steps.title: a prompt belonging to something else must not be pressed
steps.expected: FAIL. The only live prompt at the spawn belongs to `BedPrompt`, not to Tam, so `interact_with` must refuse rather than activate the wrong provider. That refusal is CD-5's S02-15 in miniature: the bed is the exact object the operator watched a segment press `interact` at 31 times through a floor.
steps.observation: EXPECTED FAIL: negative control for the provider check. A PASS means interact_with pressed a prompt belonging to something other than the entity it was given.

steps.title: get out of bed, the way a player does
steps.expected: the bed's own prompt is live and belongs to the bed, so the press happens and something changes. Named with `expect_prompt` and no `entity`: this step is about the prompt that IS live, which is the other half of what interact_with is for.

steps.title: DIAG: out of the house, onto open ground by the well
steps.expected: the player stands on open ground a short walk from Tam. See this file's `_comment_why_diag`: leaving the house on foot is past what stick_navigator.gd does, and proving that is not this segment's job.

steps.title: the teleport landed on the ground
steps.expected: the player is where the jump said, standing on the terrain rather than falling through it

steps.title: walk to Tam, tracking his live position
steps.expected: the walk resolves Tam by node name, re-reads his position every frame, and ends within 2 m of him IN 3D -- not within 2 m of where he stood when this file was written, and not 3 m above him

steps.title: still in the world after the walk
steps.expected: nothing took input during the walk. If a conversation opened on the way, this says so HERE rather than letting the next step press into it.

steps.title: the prompt is live, and it is Tam's
steps.expected: interaction_arbiter.gd offers 'Greet Tam', the winning provider is part of Tam, and the press changes something. A press that changed nothing is a FAIL: that is the 31-interacts-through-a-floor case.

steps.title: greeting Tam opened his conversation
steps.expected: input_context is 'narrative_modal': the press reached dialogue_panel.gd rather than doing nothing

steps.title: advance the conversation by predicate until it closes
steps.expected: the panel's own line is read, pressed past, and the loop stops the moment is_open() goes false -- never a guessed press count, and never a press after close, which would re-open the conversation through the interaction arbiter (CD-3)

steps.title: input came back
steps.expected: CD-3's own regression, verbatim: after any dialogue step, input_context must not be 'narrative_modal'

steps.title: walk to a harvest node, resolved by point-of-interest kind
steps.expected: the second of CD-5's three named targets. Harvest nodes are scattered in their hundreds and none has a name worth writing down, so this resolves by the same script-path table gate_f_probe.gd::_poi_kind uses for the dead-travel meter. The nearest is picked and the result says how many matched. `within` is 1.5 m and not 2.5: harvest_node.gd configures its Interactable at a 2.4 m radius, from a prompt node sitting 0.6 m above the node's origin, so a walk that stopped at 2.5 m in 3D was outside the game's own reach. The first run of this segment asked for 2.5 and SC-R-15 correctly refused to press -- which is interact_with earning its keep on the segment author rather than on the game.

steps.title: the harvest prompt is live, and the press reaches it
steps.expected: a live prompt from the node the walk arrived at -- "Strip meadow grass" -- and a press that reaches its provider. `expect_change: false`, written down in advance and for a reason: the player boots with an empty satchel and nothing equipped, and harvest_node.gd's `_on_gathered` refuses a bare-handed press for a resource that needs a tool, leaving the node where it is. So there is nothing for _cell_snapshot to see, and the acknowledgement is the honest verdict. What this step still proves is the whole of what it is here for: within the game's own 2.4 m radius the arbiter offers a prompt, interact_with presses it, and outside that radius the same step refuses to press at all.
steps.observation: Whether a bare-handed refusal is LEGIBLE to a player -- the press produces no context, focus, satchel, build, party or flag change that this harness can observe -- is a question about the game, and an instrument check must not pretend to answer it. Recorded in ralph/reports/gate-f-rig-log.md as a candidate for a journey segment to look at with a HUD frame.

steps.title: close the segment

args.text: SC-R-03 and SC-R-04 are EXPECTED FAILs and are the negative controls for _find_entity and for interact_with's provider check. Every other FAIL here is a real one. INVENTORY.json's `derails` array records any derail even after a resync, so a segment that lost the thread and found it again cannot close looking clean.

steps.expected: a note event closes the segment
